title: CPG-512: polynomial-copy correlation decoding with cutoff Grover search

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CPG-512 configuration specified in proof.md uses m=512(n+2) independent ideal coset copies and returns the entire s with unconditional probability at least 2/3. In the protected uniform Clifford+T/classical-bit-operation model, the worst-case total work bound on every execution branch is T=O(2^(n/2) n^20), with an absolute outer constant and exactly the growth index 1. All acquisitions, failed outcomes, preprocessing, finite-precision gate synthesis, addressing, initialization and retained circuit/work storage are charged as in proof.md; the four resource guarantees and clean-input success hold jointly for this same configuration. The complete representative structured envelope is the declared bound below; its outer coefficient 1 denotes big-O normalization only. No record, frontier dominance, historical novelty or 2^(O(n^(1/3))) research-goal claim is made.

The guaranteed malformed-sample fraction is epsilon(n)=0 under the error model below: every acquired copy is independent ideal rho_s for the same unknown s, and no malformed copy is allowed. With at most floor(0*Q)=0 malformed copies the same algorithm and configuration has unconditional full-secret success at least 2/3 jointly with all four declared all-branch resource bounds, including internal gate-approximation error. No positive source-corruption tolerance or impossibility of greater tolerance is claimed.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
